name: Woodcut
summary: A relief print that carves itself: every frame is a black wood block inside a warm paper margin, and light exists only where a gouge has cut it away; sweeps, ray bursts and form-following hatching are cut stroke by stroke, titles are carved out of black panels, captions are letterpress in the margin, and one colour plate (Prussian blue here) prints only inside the cuts of the one thing that matters.

palette.use: warm laid paper: carved whites and the margin
ink: the uncut block and the letterpress captions
the colour plate of this film (cold Prussian blue): printed only inside cuts, for the one thing that matters (the blue light) (proposed hex)
the source's copper plate, for heat stories (molten metal, fire); a film uses one plate, never both
the wood block itself, only in shots that show the block
small letterpress credits in the margin (ink thinned) (proposed)
the paper's laid lines and fibres (proposed)

type.case: carved titles in small capitals; captions in sentence case
type.emphasis: italic in captions; in the block, the colour plate printed in the carved letters

banned: copperplate engraving: no swelling burin lines on white, no crosshatch built up from a white ground
linocut poster art with flat colour areas
a photo run through a threshold filter: cuts follow form
fades in, dissolves: things are carved, prints are pulled
colour sitting on black; a decorative colour plate; two colour plates
hatching on every surface (it reads as fur or rain); grey on grey
text over the picture (only carved out of an uncut black panel, or letterpress in the margin)
black faces with white cuts at small sizes
copying named printmakers' plates, figures, borders or titles
